policies.description: Only users with Administrator, Manager, or Agent roles may create a knowledge‑incident link; users with the Reporter role may not.
references: Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge. READ access to all the tables. Can update assignment, state, and resolution.

Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. Can reassign incidents/requests. Can approve/reject Change Requests. Monitors SLAs and escalations.
Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Reporter (reporter) | IT Service Consumption | Cannot view or modify records opened by other users, CMDB, or internal work notes.

policies.description: Every knowledge‑incident link must record the `used_as` type, which must be one of the allowed values: suggested, applied, or resolution.
references: Use Tracking: All knowledge links must track used_as type: suggested, applied, or resolution.

policies.description: A knowledge article must be in the `published` state before it can be linked to an incident.
references: Article Status: Only articles in knowledge.state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.

policies.description: Do not assume or fabricate `incident_id` or `knowledge_id`; both identifiers must be verified to exist via API results before creating the link.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: The link creation must be performed as a single validated operation; no other actions should be bundled with it.
references: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.description: All mandatory fields for the link operation (`incident_id` and `knowledge_id`) must be present and non‑empty before invoking the tool.
references: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: When an Incident is created, the system must automatically perform a knowledge search for relevant articles.
references: When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.

policies.description: For any matching article found during incident creation, the system must create an incident‑knowledge link with `used_as = suggested`.
references: When an Incident is created, a search for relevant knowledge must be performed, and matching articles linked as used_as = suggested.

policies.description: Before creating a knowledge‑incident link, verify that the Incident and the Knowledge article belong to the same organization.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: Before creating a knowledge‑incident link, verify that the requesting user has the required role‑based access to both Incident and Knowledge records.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: When creating a knowledge‑incident link, the action must be recorded as a work log that includes the timestamp (`created_on`) and the `user_id` of the assistant performing the operation.
references: Time Tracking: All work logs must include the timestamp (created_on) and the user_id performing the action.
